question: What is the primary goal of prenatal services in maternal healthcare?

options.A: Determining the exact birth weight of the infant
options.B: Speeding up the exact date of spontaneous delivery
options.C: Ensuring good health outcomes for mother and baby
options.D: Eliminating all physical discomforts of early pregnancy

explanation: Prenatal care focuses on monitoring and promoting the health of both the pregnant woman and her developing fetus. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: Why does effective prenatal care emphasize prevention over emergency treatment?

options.A: It completely removes the need for skilled attendants at birth
options.B: It ensures that labor will last for a very short duration
options.C: It prevents the normal physiological changes of pregnancy from occurring
options.D: It stops potential complications before they become life-threatening emergencies

explanation: Early identification and management of risk factors prevent minor issues from escalating into severe obstetric emergencies. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: When is the ideal time for a pregnant woman to have her first antenatal booking visit?
explanation: Early booking in the first trimester allows baseline health assessments and timely implementation of preventive measures. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of risk stratification during antenatal visits?

options.A: To assign the pregnant woman to the correct level of healthcare facility
options.B: To decide whether the mother needs nutritional supplements
options.C: To determine the exact gender of the unborn baby
options.D: To calculate the total hospital expenses before delivery

explanation: Stratifying risk ensures that high-risk mothers receive care from specialized personnel in well-equipped centers. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: Which laboratory test is routinely performed during the initial antenatal visit to check for anemia?
explanation: Hemoglobin levels are measured early to detect and manage maternal anemia promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Why is taking a detailed obstetric history important during the first prenatal appointment?

options.A: It stops the mother from experiencing morning sickness
options.B: It reveals complications from past pregnancies that might recur
options.C: It predicts the exact day labor will begin
options.D: It determines the baby's blood group before birth

explanation: Past obstetric history, such as previous postpartum hemorrhage or pre-eclampsia, guides current monitoring strategies. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: What physical measurement is used at each follow-up visit to monitor fetal growth against gestational age?
explanation: Measuring fundal height provides a reliable, quick estimation of fetal growth progression during routine visits. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: Why must nurses routinely test maternal urine during follow-up antenatal visits?

options.A: To confirm the mother's daily caloric consumption
options.B: To measure the exact volume of daily fluid intake
options.C: To diagnose fetal chromosomal abnormalities early
options.D: To detect protein or glucose indicating potential complications

explanation: Proteinuria suggests pre-eclampsia, while glucosuria can indicate gestational diabetes, requiring prompt follow-up. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: What type of food is particularly emphasized in pregnancy nutrition counseling for preventing anemia?

options.A: High-sugar snacks for quick energy boosts
options.B: Green leafy vegetables and iron-rich foods
options.C: Processed canned foods for long preservation
options.D: High-fat dairy products for bone density

explanation: Iron-rich foods and green leafy vegetables provide essential nutrients necessary to prevent maternal anemia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: Why is it important to explain pregnancy warning signs using simple local terms?

options.A: To replace the need for professional medical check-ups at the hospital
options.B: To ensure the mother and her family recognize emergencies and seek help quickly
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing prescribed drugs
options.D: To help the mother calculate her expected date of delivery easily

explanation: Clear, jargon-free communication ensures prompt action when dangerous symptoms like bleeding or severe headaches occur. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: Which immunization is routinely given during antenatal care to prevent a fatal infection in the newborn?
explanation: Tetanus toxoid vaccination protects the newborn against neonatal tetanus infection contracted through the umbilical cord. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: What is the appropriate nursing action when a pregnant woman presents with signs of severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Stabilize the patient and arrange immediate transfer to an emergency facility
options.B: Advise her to walk around the clinic compound to lower her blood pressure
options.C: Send her home with instructions to return for her next scheduled appointment
options.D: Prescribe herbal teas and tell her to rest in a dark room

explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia requires immediate stabilization and emergency referral to prevent seizures or stroke. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: What is a key component of an individual birth plan created during antenatal visits?

options.A: Arranging reliable transportation to the delivery facility
options.B: Deciding the exact name of the baby before birth
options.C: Choosing the exact career path for the unborn child
options.D: Purchasing baby clothes of a specific designer brand

explanation: A birth plan specifically includes logistical preparations like transport to prevent delays during labor. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Why is discussing postpartum family planning during antenatal care beneficial?

options.A: It guarantees that the next pregnancy will be a multiple birth
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum blues
options.C: It stops milk production immediately after the baby is born
options.D: It gives parents time to make informed choices about birth spacing before delivery

explanation: Discussing family planning early prepares couples to space subsequent pregnancies safely for optimal maternal health. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: What portable medical document does a pregnant woman carry with her throughout her antenatal visits?
explanation: The antenatal card serves as the primary portable record containing vital health data for emergency and routine visits. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)

question: Why is a structured referral system essential within the Nigerian healthcare framework for pregnant women?

options.A: It facilitates smooth transfer of high-risk cases from primary clinics to higher-level hospitals
options.B: It eliminates the need for keeping written records in secondary facilities
options.C: It ensures that patients never have to pay for healthcare services
options.D: It allows primary health centers to handle all major surgical procedures safely

explanation: A structured referral system connects lower-level clinics to specialized centers, ensuring timely care for complex cases. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)
